custom_logic_notes: The EA uses a TSI (True Strength Index) MACD custom indicator which is not a built-in MT5 indicator. The TSI calculation involves double-smoothing of momentum: first smoothing the absolute momentum and the signed momentum separately, then dividing. The MACD variant adds a signal line crossover. The SmoothAlgorithms.mqh library provides multiple smoothing methods (SMA, EMA, SMMA, LWMA, JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) - the default EMA is used here but any can be selected. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library handles position open/close with margin mode calculation, deviation control, and global variable management. Signal logic: compares Ind[1] vs Sign[1] (previous bar) to determine trend state, then checks Ind[0] vs Sign[0] (signal bar) to detect crossover. Entry only when crossover confirmed on SignalBar=1 (previous completed bar). BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose input booleans control which directions are enabled.
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement TSI_MACD indicator from scratch: 1) Calculate price series per Applied_price_ enum (default Close), 2) Compute momentum = price[t] - price[t-MomPeriod], 3) Double-smooth: first smooth momentum and |momentum| with XFast period EMA, then smooth again with XSlow period EMA, 4) TSI = 100 * double_smoothed_momentum / double_smoothed_|momentum|, 5) MACD line = TSI, Signal = EMA(TSI, XLength3) — actually the TSI_MACD likely computes as: fast TSI - slow TSI or similar MACD construction. The exact formula requires reading the TSI_MACD indicator source code. TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose) must be replaced with simple market order logic with SL/TP in points. Signal detection uses 2-bar lookback: Ind[1]>Sign[1] (trend state) + Ind[0]<=Sign[0] (crossover trigger). New bar guard via CIsNewBar class must be reimplemented. Position sizing with MarginMode=LOT simplifies to fixed lot=0.1.
